name: Cranberry-Orange Muffins with Rosemary

about: Low-sugar, gluten-free cranberry-orange muffins made with oats, almond flour and tahini, with a little fresh rosemary. Adapted from The Plant-Based Cookbook: Vegan, Gluten-Free, Oil-Free Recipes for Lifelong Health.
instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 350°F and line or grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
2. Stir the psyllium husk into the water and leave it about 5 minutes to gel.
3. In a large bowl, whisk together the almond flour, oat flour, oats, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt, breaking up any lumps.
4. Blend the almond milk, applesauce, orange zest and juice, tahini, maple syrup, vanilla and the psyllium gel until smooth.
5. Pour the wet mix into the dry and stir just until there are no dry patches, then fold in the cranberries and rosemary.
6. Divide among the 12 cups (about ½ cup each) and bake 23–26 minutes, until the tops feel nearly firm.
7. Let them cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then loosen the edges and move them to a rack.

name: Everyday Overnight Oats
about: Half overnight oats, half chia pudding: five minutes the night before and breakfast is waiting in the fridge. Good in a jar to take with you. Top with fruit, the Cinnamon-Spiced House Granola, or a spoon of nut butter. Adapted from The Plant-Based Cookbook: Vegan, Gluten-Free, Oil-Free Recipes for Lifelong Health.
instructions:
1. In a large lidded container, combine the oats, chia, berries and cinnamon.
2. Pour in the milk and vanilla, plus maple syrup if you want it sweeter, and stir well.
3. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
4. In the morning give it a stir, loosen with a splash more milk if it's thick, and spoon into bowls with any toppings.
5. Prefer it warm? Heat a portion gently on the stove.

Tip: frozen berries will tint the milk as they thaw.

name: Rise n' Shine Smoothie Bowl
about: A thick, spoonable smoothie with banana, mango or berries, spinach and seeds. Add more milk to drink it as a smoothie instead. Nice toppings: granola, chia, goji or fresh berries, shredded coconut. Adapted from The Plant-Based Cookbook: Vegan, Gluten-Free, Oil-Free Recipes for Lifelong Health.
instructions:
1. Put everything in the blender, liquid first and frozen fruit last.
2. Blend on high until thick and smooth, pushing it down with the tamper as needed. Add a little more milk to thin it, or hold back milk for a thicker bowl.
3. Split between two bowls and add your toppings.

ingredients.originalLine: 1 cup frozen mango or mixed berries

name: Raw Green Buckwheat Bowl
about: Buckwheat groats soaked overnight, then blended with banana, almond milk and a handful of greens you won't taste. Small servings but filling. Skip the almond butter for a lighter or nut-free bowl, or swap the spinach for kale. Adapted from The Plant-Based Cookbook: Vegan, Gluten-Free, Oil-Free Recipes for Lifelong Health.
instructions:
1. The night before, cover the buckwheat with a few inches of water in a bowl, drape a clean towel over it and leave it to soak (counter or fridge).
2. In the morning, tip it into a fine strainer and rinse well. The soaking water is thick and slow to drain; that's normal, so give it a few minutes and throw it away.
3. Blend the almond milk, banana, sweetener (maple or dates), spinach, flax, almond butter and cinnamon until smooth.
4. Add the drained buckwheat and blend again, briefly for some texture or longer for smooth. Thin with more milk if needed.
5. Serve in bowls topped with berries and sliced banana.

name: Sunshine Smoothie
about: A bright yellow smoothie with pineapple, banana, turmeric and fresh ginger, plus flax and hemp. Use water instead of almond milk to keep it nut-free, swap the pineapple for frozen blueberries for a blue version, or add a handful of spinach or kale. Adapted from The Plant-Based Cookbook: Vegan, Gluten-Free, Oil-Free Recipes for Lifelong Health.
instructions:
1. Add everything to the blender, liquid first.
2. Blend on high, adding more milk a splash at a time until it's as thick or thin as you like.

Green option: add a packed cup of spinach or kale before blending.

instructions:

2. Start on low and blend about 1 minute, then turn it up to high and blend another 1–2 minutes, until completely smooth and creamy. A regular blender may need longer and a splash more water.

ingredients.notes: in a squeeze pouch or small jar
boiling, or cold to soak overnight

instructions:
At home: bag everything except the peanut butter and water.

At camp: add 1¼ cups boiling water, stir, cover and wait 5 minutes. Stir in the peanut butter.

No stove: add cold water in the evening and let it soak overnight.

name: Thai Peanut Couscous
instructions:
At home: bag the couscous, seeds, coconut, peanuts and spices together. Carry the peanut butter separately.

At camp: stir the peanut butter into ¾ cup boiling water, pour it over the couscous mix, cover and wait 5 minutes. Fluff and eat.

name: Southwest Bean Bowl
instructions:
At home: bag the beans, rice and seasoning together; bag the hemp hearts, sunflower seeds, nutritional yeast and chips separately so they stay crunchy.

At camp: add 1¼ cups boiling water to the beans and rice, stir, cover and wait 8–10 minutes. Top with the seeds, nutritional yeast and chips.

name: Coconut Curry Red Lentils
instructions:
Red lentils need about 15 minutes of simmering. To save fuel, cook and dehydrate them at home, or use red lentil flakes; then just add boiling water and wait 10 minutes.

At camp: simmer the lentils, mushrooms and spices in 1½ cups water until soft, then stir in the peanut butter and coconut.

Check labels if you need it to be strictly gluten-free (curry powder and lentils are usually fine).

name: Loaded Mashed Potatoes
instructions:
At home: bag the potato flakes, nutritional yeast, mushrooms, green onion, pepper and salt together. Carry the hemp hearts and tahini separately.

At camp: add 1 cup boiling water, stir and wait 3–5 minutes for the mushrooms to soften. Stir in the tahini and top with hemp hearts.

name: Taco Mushroom Ramen

ingredients.notes: Top Ramen; use half the seasoning packet or less

instructions:
At home: bag the noodles, mushrooms, cabbage, corn and seasonings together; bag the hemp hearts and sunflower seeds separately.

At camp: bring 1½ cups water to a boil, add everything except the toppings and simmer 3 minutes (or cover off the heat for 5). Top with hemp hearts, sunflower seeds and a squeeze of lime if you have one.
about: A “campfire taco soup” take on ramen, good as an after-ceremony meal. Let the taco seasoning be the main flavour; the ramen packet and taco seasoning are both salty, so go light on the packet.

name: Peanut Ramen
instructions: At camp: cook the noodles and mushrooms in 1¾ cups boiling water for 3 minutes. Stir the peanut butter and spices into the broth until creamy, then top with hemp hearts.

name: Sweet Crunch Wrap
instructions:
Spread the peanut butter almost to the edges of the tortilla, scatter everything else over it, roll up and eat. No cooking.

Tip: a thin tortilla with a generous filling keeps the calories per gram high.

name: Southwest Bean Wrap
instructions: Stir the water into the bean flakes and seasoning and let it sit 5 minutes (hot water is faster). Spread on the tortilla, top with hemp hearts, nutritional yeast and chips, and roll up.

name: Savory Mushroom Wrap
instructions: Soak the mushrooms and cabbage in the water for 10 minutes (hot water is faster), then drain. Spread the tahini on the tortilla, add the vegetables, nutritional yeast and pepper, and roll up.

name: Classic Trail Mix
instructions: Mix and divide into 4 bags of about ½ cup each.

name: Peanut Butter Stuffed Dates
instructions: Slit each date, fill with peanut butter and press closed. Pack in a small container so they don't squash.

name: Date-Walnut Energy Balls
instructions: Pulse the walnuts and oats in a food processor until coarse, add the dates, flax, cinnamon and salt and process until it sticks together. Roll into 12 balls. They keep about a week somewhere cool.

name: Muhammara

ingredients.ingredient: Aleppo-style pepper, Maras red pepper flakes, or other mild chile flakes
ingredients.notes: Maras red pepper flakes, or other mild chile flakes

ingredients.ingredient: pomegranate molasses, plus more for drizzling

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Dips + Sauces). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Bon Appétit; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Set a rack in the upper third of the oven and heat it to 350°F. Spread the walnuts on a rimmed baking sheet and toast 8–10 minutes, tossing halfway, until golden. Let them cool, then chop a small handful coarsely and set aside for the top. Put the rest in a food processor.
2. Turn on the broiler. Broil the whole red peppers on a rimmed baking sheet for 12–15 minutes, turning now and then, until the skins are charred all over and the flesh is soft. (You can also char them directly over a gas flame on medium-high, turning with tongs.)
3. Put the hot peppers in a bowl, cover tightly with plastic wrap and leave 10 minutes; the steam loosens the skins. Peel them (a few stubborn bits of skin are fine) and pull out the seeds and ribs.
4. Add the peppers to the food processor with the walnuts, breadcrumbs, mild chile flakes (Aleppo or Maras), olive oil, pomegranate molasses, tahini, lemon juice and paprika. Pulse, rather than run continuously, until mostly smooth with a little texture. Season with salt.
5. Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with a little more pomegranate molasses and scatter the chopped walnuts on top.

Keeps up to 4 days in an airtight container in the fridge, and tastes better after a few hours.

name: Thai Peanut Dressing

ingredients.ingredient: low sodium soy sauce, tamari or coconut aminos

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Dips + Sauces). Steps written in our own words, adapted from The Modern Proper; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Put the soy sauce, peanut butter, fish sauce, vegetable oil, lime juice, vinegar, honey and sugar in a small bowl.
2. Whisk hard (or blend) for 2–4 minutes, until completely smooth and the sugar has dissolved; it takes longer than you'd think for the peanut butter to loosen.

Keeps up to 1 week in an airtight container in the fridge.

name: Ginger Garlic Miso Tahini Sauce

heaping tsp yellow or white miso paste ((use chickpea miso for soy-free
toasted or untoasted sesame oil ((if oil-free, sub water

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Dips + Sauces). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Minimalist Baker; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. In a medium bowl, whisk together the tahini, grated ginger, garlic, miso, coconut aminos, rice vinegar, sesame oil and maple syrup. It will seize up and get thick at first; that's normal.
2. Whisk in water a little at a time until the sauce is creamy and pourable.
3. Taste and adjust: more vinegar for tang, maple for sweetness, miso for depth, garlic or ginger for bite, or salt/coconut aminos for saltiness.

Keeps 5–7 days in the fridge, or freeze up to 1 month (best fresh).

name: Green Goddess
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Dips + Sauces). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Love and Lemons; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Put the yogurt, parsley, mixed herbs, chives, lemon juice and zest, olive oil, capers, garlic, salt and pepper in a food processor.
2. Pulse until the herbs are finely chopped and everything is evenly green and combined. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
3. Serve as a dip or toss through salad greens.

Keeps up to 5 days in an airtight container in the fridge.

name: Sundried Tomato and Almond Pesto

ingredients.ingredient: oil from jar of sun-dried tomatoes

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Dips + Sauces). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Pick Up Limes; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat a small dry pan over medium-high and toast the almonds 4–5 minutes, stirring constantly so they don't scorch, until fragrant and lightly browned.
2. Put the toasted almonds and all the remaining ingredients in a food processor. Blend, scraping down the sides once or twice, until it's a thick, mostly smooth paste.
3. Serve with crackers or spread on sandwiches.

name: Jalapeño Cashew Cream Sauce

ingredients.ingredient: water, plus 2 tablespoons more if necessary

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Dips + Sauces). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Ambitious Kitchen; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Soak the cashews in 2 cups warm water for at least 2 hours. Quick method: put the cashews in a pot of water over high heat, bring to a boil, turn off the heat immediately and let them sit in the hot water 30 minutes.
2. Drain the cashews and discard the soaking water.
3. Put the cashews in a blender with fresh water, the jalapeño, garlic, lemon juice, salt, onion powder and black pepper. Blend on high until completely smooth.
4. For a thinner sauce, blend in 1–2 more tablespoons water.

Makes about 1 cup (serves 4).

name: Pumpkin Seed Dressing
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Dips + Sauces). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Cooking for Peanuts; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Soak the pumpkin seeds: 15 minutes in hot water, or at least 4 hours (or overnight) in room-temperature water. Drain well.
2. Put the drained seeds in a high-speed blender with the tahini, capers, garlic, parsley, tarragon, chives, lemon juice, miso, water, salt and pepper. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. (No high-speed blender? Use an immersion blender in a wide-mouth jar or deep container.)
3. Taste and add more lemon, salt or pepper as needed. Blend in a splash more water if you want it thinner and more pourable.

name: Crunchy Almond and Mango Granola
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Sides + Snax). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Pick Up Limes; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C) and line a large baking tray with parchment.
2. In a large bowl, stir together all the dry ingredients (everything except the mango and hemp seeds).
3. In a medium bowl, whisk the wet ingredients until smooth and glossy, like a thin caramel.
4. Pour the wet mixture over the dry and stir until everything is evenly coated.
5. Spread it out on the tray in an even layer. Bake on the middle rack about 30 minutes, stirring once halfway, until lightly golden.
6. Let cool on the tray without stirring; it crisps up as it cools. Then toss in the dried mango and hemp seeds.
7. Once completely cool, store in an airtight container. Serve with fruit and yogurt or milk.

name: Tachin/Tahdig Iranian Crispy Saffron Rice

ingredients.ingredient: barberries or 1 cup dried tart cherries
grapeseed or vegetable oil, plus more for dish
ingredients.notes: grapeseed or vegetable, plus more for dish

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Sides + Snax). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Bon Appétit; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Bring a large pot of water to a boil with a big handful of salt (about ½ cup). Meanwhile, rinse the rice in a sieve under lukewarm water, swishing with your hand, until the water runs clear.
2. Add the rice to the boiling water and stir a few times so it doesn't stick. Cook 6–8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the grains rise to the top and are tender outside but still have a slight bite. Drain and rinse with cold water.
3. Melt the butter in a small skillet over medium-low. Add the barberries and stir for about 2 minutes, until slightly plump and warm. Take off the heat and stir in the rose water, if using.
4. Set a rack in the lower third of the oven and heat to 400°F. In a large bowl, steep the saffron in 2 tablespoons hot water for 10 minutes so it gives up its colour. Whisk in the egg yolks, yogurt, ½ cup oil and 2 teaspoons salt. Add the rice and fold gently until every grain is coated.
5. Oil a 10-inch glass pie dish (glass lets you check the colour underneath). Add half the rice and press it down firmly with your palms or the bottom of a measuring cup. Scatter over half the barberries, add the rest of the rice and press down again, harder this time; a tight pack helps it turn out in one piece.
6. Cover tightly with foil and bake 65–80 minutes, until the bottom and sides are deep golden brown.
7. Let it sit 10 minutes, then remove the foil and run a knife around the edge. Put a large plate on top and flip it over, like turning out a cake. Scatter the remaining barberries on top.

name: Korean Drug “Mayak” Eggs

ingredients.ingredient: green onions, seaweed flakes, and/or sesame oil
ingredients.notes: seaweed flakes, and/or sesame oil (for garnish, optional)
corn syrup, oligo syrup, or your choice of liquid sweetener

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Sides + Snax). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Cookerru; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Mix all the marinade ingredients in a bowl or lidded container, scraping the honey off the bottom so it dissolves.
2. Bring a pot of water to a boil and add the vinegar and salt. Lower to a gentle simmer and lower the eggs in one at a time with a spoon. Simmer 6 minutes for jammy yolks (10 minutes for hard-boiled). Meanwhile, fill a large bowl with ice water.
3. As soon as the timer goes, move the eggs straight into the ice water and leave 5–10 minutes until completely cold.
4. Peel gently and put the eggs in the marinade. Cover tightly and refrigerate at least 6 hours, ideally overnight.
5. Serve over rice (or noodles) with a spoonful of the marinade, topped with green onion, seaweed flakes and/or a drizzle of sesame oil.

name: Red Potato Salad

ingredients.notes: plus more for cooking the potatoes
chopped (plus more for garnish), chopped, fresh

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Sides + Snax). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Love and Lemons; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water by 1 inch and stir in 2 tablespoons salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then lower to a simmer and cook 5–10 minutes, until a fork slides in easily. Drain and let cool slightly.
2. In a medium bowl, whisk together the olive oil, mustard, lemon juice, mayo, vinegar, garlic, salt and plenty of black pepper.
3. Put the warm potatoes in a large bowl, pour over the dressing and stir to coat (warm potatoes soak it up better). Add the celery, scallions, chives and dill and stir again.
4. Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour so the flavours come together.
5. Before serving, taste and add salt or more lemon juice. Garnish with extra chives.

name: Orange Oat Chocolate Bars
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Brekky). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Pick Up Limes; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Toast the pecans in a dry pan over medium-high for 3–5 minutes, stirring often, until fragrant and lightly toasted.
2. Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and line a 10×7-inch (26×17 cm) baking dish with parchment.
3. Pulse the dried apricots and toasted pecans in a food processor until broken into small chunks.
4. Tip into a large bowl and add the oats, almond flour, cinnamon, orange zest (keep a little for the top) and salt. Stir well.
5. Add the peanut butter, maple syrup and vanilla and mix until it holds together.
6. Press the mixture into the dish as firmly as you can and level it out; firm pressing keeps the bars from crumbling.
7. Bake on the middle rack 25–30 minutes, until lightly golden on top. Cool a few minutes in the dish, then lift out with the parchment and cool completely.
8. Melt the chocolate (microwave in short bursts, or in a bowl over simmering water) and drizzle it over the bars. Sprinkle with sea salt and the reserved orange zest.
9. Once the chocolate sets, cut into 8 squares or about 10 bars.

name: Sweet Potato Quinoa Oat Bars
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Brekky). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Abbey's Kitchen; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 350°F. Line two 9×5-inch loaf pans with parchment.
2. Stir the ground flax into the water in a small bowl and leave 20 minutes to thicken into a flax egg.
3. In a large bowl, mix the oats, cooked quinoa, baking powder, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg.
4. Add the mashed sweet potato, almond butter, maple syrup, flax egg and vanilla and mix until smooth and evenly combined. Fold in the dried cherries and coconut.
5. Divide between the two pans and smooth the tops with a spatula.
6. Bake on the middle rack about 25 minutes, until the edges are browned.
7. Let cool completely in the pans (they firm up as they cool), then lift out onto a board and cut into squares.
8. For the topping, microwave the chocolate chips with the coconut oil in 30-second bursts, stirring between, until melted. Stir in the almond butter until very smooth. Drizzle or pipe over the cut bars.

Keeps 3–4 days in an airtight container.

name: Buckwheat Pancakes
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Brekky). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Pick Up Limes; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Mash the bananas well in a large bowl.
2. Add the rest of the ingredients and stir until combined. If the batter seems runny, let it sit 5 minutes to thicken.
3. Heat a large nonstick pan over medium and add a little oil.
4. Once hot, drop about 2 tablespoons of batter per pancake and use the back of the spoon to spread it into a round.
5. Cook until the bottom is lightly golden and the edges look set, then flip and cook the other side. Turn the heat down a bit if they brown before cooking through.
6. Serve with your favourite toppings.

name: Quinoa Rice Pudding
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Brekky). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Darn Good Veggies; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. In a large saucepan, combine the mashed banana, almond milk, coconut milk, maple syrup and salt. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
2. Stir in the cooked rice and quinoa. Keep simmering, stirring often so it doesn't catch on the bottom, for 10–12 minutes, until thick and very creamy.
3. Take off the heat and stir in the cinnamon, vanilla and almond extract.
4. Spoon into bowls and add your toppings.

name: Oat and Cranberry Breakfast Bars

ingredients.notes: I used extra virgin olive oil but for a lighter flavor choose a light colored olive oil
dried, finely chopped (select brand with low FODMAP ingredients), chopped, finely

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Brekky). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Kate Scarlata; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 350°F. Line an 8×8-inch square pan with parchment.
2. In a medium bowl, mix the oil, brown sugar, eggs and extract until blended.
3. Stir in the oats and oat flour.
4. Fold in the pepitas, shredded coconut, sunflower seeds and cranberries.
5. Tip into the pan and press down firmly and evenly with the back of a wooden spoon; packing it tight keeps the bars from crumbling.
6. Bake 20 minutes. Let cool completely in the pan, then cut into 12 bars.

name: Savory Chickpea Pancake

ingredients.notes: also known as garbanzo flour or besan

ingredients.ingredient: For serving: salsa, avocado, hummus, cashew cream

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Brekky). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Oh She Glows; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Chop the vegetables finely and set aside. Put a 10-inch skillet over medium heat to preheat.
2. In a small bowl, whisk the chickpea flour, garlic powder, salt, pepper, baking powder and red pepper flakes (if using).
3. Add the water and whisk hard for a good 15 seconds, until there are no lumps and the batter is full of little bubbles.
4. Stir in the chopped vegetables.
5. When a drop of water sizzles on the skillet, spray or brush it generously with olive oil.
6. Pour in all the batter (for one large pancake) and quickly spread it to the edges. Cook 5–6 minutes, until a spatula slides easily underneath and the pancake is firm enough to flip without breaking.
7. Flip carefully and cook about 5 minutes more, until lightly golden. Give it the full time; it takes much longer than a regular pancake.
8. Slide onto a plate and add toppings. Leftovers keep wrapped in the fridge; reheat in a skillet.

name: Frozen Yogurt Oat Breakfast Bars
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Brekky). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Pick Up Limes; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Put the frozen berries in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring now and then, until thawed, juicy and heated through. Take off the heat.
2. Blend the dates in a food processor until smooth and sticky.
3. Add the oats, almond butter, ground flaxseed and cinnamon and blend again until well combined.
4. Press the mixture firmly into a parchment-lined 11×7-inch (18×28 cm) baking dish. The harder you press, the better the bars hold together.
5. Spread the yogurt evenly over the base.
6. Spoon dots of the stewed berries over the yogurt and swirl with a butter knife.
7. Freeze 1–2 hours, until solid enough to cut.
8. Cut into squares or bars and let them sit 3–5 minutes before eating. Store extras in the freezer.

name: Tempeh, Sausage, and Potato Hash
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Brekky). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Nikki Vegan; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil over medium-high in a large frying pan that has a lid. Add the scallions and cauliflower, then crumble in the tempeh with your fingers. Add a pinch of salt and cook 2–3 minutes.
2. Stir in the taco seasoning, nutritional yeast, turmeric, salt and black pepper. (If your taco seasoning already has salt, cut the salt to ¼ teaspoon and adjust at the end.)
3. Add the potatoes and water, stir, and put the lid on. Turn the heat down to medium and cook about 15 minutes, until the potatoes are fork-tender and the water is absorbed.
4. Stir in the chopped cilantro. Taste and add more salt and pepper; it should taste bold.
5. Top with salsa verde. Good with avocado toast and fruit, wrapped in tortillas, or spooned warm over an arugula salad with cucumber, avocado and a squeeze of lemon.

1. Heat the oven to 375°F.
2. For the topping, stir the oats, cinnamon and salt together in a mixing bowl. Mash the banana and add it with the almond butter and maple syrup. Mix well, then stir in the pecans.
3. Toss the berries with the flour until evenly coated, then spread them in a baking dish.
4. Spoon the oat mixture over the berries.
5. Bake about 45 minutes, until golden and bubbling at the edges. It can look done at 30 minutes; give it the full time so the top crisps.
6. Serve warm with unsweetened yogurt, a drizzle of almond butter and fresh fruit, or with ice cream or coconut whipped cream as a dessert.

2. In a medium bowl, mash the bananas until smooth. Whisk in the milk, espresso (or strong coffee), maple syrup, nut butter, vanilla and apple cider vinegar.
3. In a large bowl, stir together the rolled oats, cocoa, protein powder (if using), baking powder, baking soda and salt.
4. Pour the wet mix into the dry and stir well. Spread in the dish and smooth the top.
5. Bake 35–40 minutes, until the centre is set and the top golden. Leave to cool completely in the dish.
6. For the yogurt layer, microwave the nut butter for 10 seconds to soften, then stir in the vanilla. Mix in 1–2 tablespoons of the yogurt until smooth, then add the rest of the yogurt, the salt and the protein powder if using (it's what makes it thick and mousse-like). Taste and add a little maple if you want it sweeter.
7. Once the oats are fully cool, spread the yogurt evenly over the top. Dust with cocoa just before serving.

name: Garlicky Kale Lentil Salad

ingredients.ingredient: black beluga or French green lentils

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Salads). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Bon Appétit; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Strip the kale leaves off the stems. Stack the leaves, roll them up tightly and slice crosswise into ¼-inch ribbons; run the knife through once or twice more to shorten any long strands. Put them in a large bowl, salt, and massage with your hands for 1–2 minutes, until softer, silkier and darker.
2. Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. While it heats, prep the oil: coarsely chop the almonds; thinly slice the white parts of the scallions (save the greens); smash and peel the garlic; and use a peeler to take three 3-inch strips of lemon peel without the white pith (keep the lemon for juice). Put the scallion whites, garlic and lemon peel in a small skillet with the olive oil and stir to coat.
3. Add the lentils to the boiling water, lower to medium and simmer uncovered 20–25 minutes, until tender but still holding their shape. Taste often; they go mushy if overcooked. Drain well.
4. While the lentils cook, put the skillet over medium heat. Cook about 3 minutes, stirring now and then, until the garlic starts to brown and the lemon peel curls. Add the almonds and stir often for about 3 more minutes, until browned. Off the heat, stir in the cumin seeds and chile flakes; the hot oil toasts them.
5. Pour through a fine sieve set over a small bowl and keep the oil; it's the dressing. Spread the almond mixture (cumin seeds and all) on a paper-towel-lined plate, salt it, and let it cool; it gets crunchier as it cools.
6. Add the crumbled feta, torn pitted olives, most of the sliced scallion greens, the lemon juice and ½ teaspoon salt to the kale.
7. Add the drained lentils, the flavoured oil and half the almond mixture and toss well. Top with the rest of the almonds and scallion greens.

instructions:
1. Make the vinaigrette first: let the shallot sit in the red wine vinegar for 15 minutes, then add the olive oil, a good pinch of salt and a small pinch of pepper. Stir or shake to combine.
2. Set racks in the lower-middle and upper-middle of the oven and heat to 425°F.
3. Halve the Brussels sprouts through the stem, toss in a large bowl with about 3 tablespoons oil and some salt, and spread in a single layer on a baking sheet. Toss the carrots in the same bowl with a little more oil and salt and spread on a second sheet.
4. Lightly trim the root ends of the cauliflower and romanesco and cut each into ¾-inch slabs through the root. Drizzle about 2 tablespoons oil on a third sheet and lay the slabs flat, cauliflower on one side and romanesco on the other. Don't let pieces touch; use another pan if needed.
5. Roast 26–30 minutes. After about 12 minutes, rotate the pans and swap their rack positions. They're done when browned outside and completely tender when pierced with a knife. Let cool a few minutes.
6. Drain the beans, keeping the liquid. Dress them with 3 tablespoons vinaigrette, salt and 1 teaspoon za'atar, plus a splash of bean liquid to keep them juicy. Taste and adjust.
7. Layer the vegetables on a large platter, drizzle with vinaigrette and sprinkle with za'atar. Spoon the beans over and add big crumbles of feta.
8. Lightly dress the cilantro, dill and mint with 1 tablespoon vinaigrette and a pinch of salt, pile on top and serve right away.

Leftover vinaigrette keeps 3 days in the fridge.

name: Thai Chicken Zoodle Salad

1. In a small bowl, mix the garlic, ginger, peanut butter, lime juice and zest, soy sauce and red pepper flakes into a sauce.
2. Heat the canola oil in a large frying pan over high heat.
3. Add the zucchini noodles, carrots and bell peppers and cook 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally, just until wilted. Don't overcook or the zoodles go watery.
4. Add the cooked chicken, the sauce, cilantro and green onions and toss until everything is coated and warmed through.
5. Top with chopped peanuts and serve with lime wedges.

name: Spicy Broccoli Salad
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Salads). Steps written in our own words, adapted from PlantYou; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Cook the tempeh bacon according to its recipe or package, then let it cool and crumble or chop it.
2. Put the dressing ingredients in a jar and whisk (or shake) until smooth. Add water a little at a time until it's the thickness you like.
3. Dice the broccoli into small bite-size pieces, and dice the bell pepper, red onion and pistachios. Put them all in a large bowl with the tempeh bacon.
4. Pour the dressing over and toss well so every piece is coated. Serve right away.

1. Heat the oven to 375°F.
2. Cut the squash top to bottom into wedges about ½ inch thick (the skin of red kuri is edible, so there's no need to peel). Toss in a baking dish with olive oil and ¾ teaspoon salt.
3. Roast 30–35 minutes, flipping once halfway, until tender all the way through.
4. Meanwhile, put the kale in a large bowl with 1 tablespoon olive oil, ¼ teaspoon salt, the cumin, harissa and ½ tablespoon lemon juice. Massage with your hands for a full 5 minutes, until it softens and darkens.
5. Whisk the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.
6. Add the squash to the kale, pour the sauce over and gently toss with your hands. Plate and finish with flaky salt.

instructions:
1. Warm the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook about 3 minutes, until translucent.
2. Add the garlic, jalapeño, ginger, cumin and cayenne and cook, stirring, 3 more minutes.
3. Stir in the tomato paste, then add the diced sweet potato, peanut butter, vegetable broth and water. Stir until the peanut butter melts in, and bring to a low boil.
4. Turn down to a medium-low simmer, cover and cook 15 minutes.
5. Add the chopped collard greens, stir, cover again and cook another 15 minutes, until the greens are wilted and the sweet potato is tender.
6. Mash some of the sweet potato against the side of the pot with the back of a spoon to thicken the stew, then boil uncovered 5 more minutes.
7. Serve over rice, topped with cilantro, chopped peanuts and a squeeze of lime.

instructions:
1. Put the galangal, bruised lemongrass, crushed chilli, tomato paste, coriander stalks and roots, and kaffir lime leaves in a pot. Add the water or stock and bring to a boil.

3. Pour through a fine sieve and discard the solids (they're for flavour, not for eating). Return the broth to the pot.
4. Bring it back to a simmer, then season with the sugar, fish sauce and lime juice, tasting as you go; aim for a balance of sour, salty, hot and a little sweet.

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Soups). Steps written in our own words, adapted from The Modern Proper; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. When it's bubbling, add the onion and mushrooms. Cook about 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and translucent and the mushrooms have given off their liquid.
2. Add the stock, wine, dill, thyme, paprika, Worcestershire sauce and salt. Turn the heat to high and bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer and cook about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid has reduced by about a third.
3. In a small bowl, whisk the flour into the milk until there are no lumps at all. Pour it slowly into the soup while stirring constantly, then keep cooking about 10 minutes more, stirring now and then, until the soup thickens.
4. Take the pot off the heat (so the sour cream doesn't split) and stir in the sour cream and lemon juice until smooth.
5. Ladle into bowls and top with a small spoonful of sour cream, chopped parsley and cracked black pepper.

name: Vegan Creamy Corn Chowder
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Soups). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Sweet Potato Soul; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high. Add the onion, garlic and celery and sauté 4–5 minutes, until the onion is translucent.
2. Stir in the carrots, potatoes, corn, coconut milk, water, thyme and bouillon paste. Bring to a boil, then lower to medium-low and simmer with the lid slightly ajar for about 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
3. Take the pot off the heat and blend about a third of the soup with an immersion blender, so it's partly creamy but still chunky. (With a regular blender: transfer about a third of the soup, remove the lid's centre cap and cover the hole with a folded towel so steam can escape, blend on medium until smooth, then pour it back in.)
4. Stir in the chili flakes and pepper, and season with salt.
5. Serve right away, topped with chopped cilantro.

name: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Mains). Steps written in our own words, adapted from 100 Days of Real Food; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. In a medium bowl, mix all the dry spices together with a fork.
2. Stir in the honey, vinegar and olive oil to make a thick paste.
3. Lay the sliced onion in the bottom of the slow cooker. Put the two pieces of pork on top and spread the paste over all sides of the meat (it's fine if a lot of it slides down to the bottom).
4. Cover and cook on LOW for 7–8 hours, until the pork is tender enough to pull apart easily with a fork.
5. Shred the pork with two forks right in the cooker and stir it through the juices. Serve warm with coleslaw, cornbread and hot sauce on the side.

Leftovers keep in the fridge, or freeze well.

name: Sun-Dried Tomato and Roasted Vegetable Tart
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Mains). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Pick Up Limes; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the oil in a large pan over high heat. Add the onions and garlic and cook 2–3 minutes.
2. Add the peas, sun-dried tomatoes, oregano, parsley, basil, salt and pepper and cook 2–3 minutes more, until most of the moisture has cooked off.
3. Transfer to a food processor with the hummus and most of the breadcrumbs (save a little) and blend until smooth.
4. Grease a 9½-inch (25 cm) round tart pan and lay the puff pastry in it. Press it gently into the bottom and up the sides to about 3 cm high, leaving the excess hanging over.
5. Prick the base all over with a fork and sprinkle with the reserved breadcrumbs (they stop the base going soggy).
6. Spread the filling evenly over the base with the back of a spoon.
7. Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Use a vegetable peeler to cut the zucchini and carrots into long thin ribbons.
8. Press the ribbons into the filling in a spiral, working from the outside in (or the centre out). Fold the overhanging pastry in over the edge to form a crust.
9. Brush the vegetables and pastry with oil. Bake on the middle rack 40–45 minutes, until the crust is golden.
10. Let it rest at least 10 minutes before cutting; it firms up as it cools.

name: Chickpea and Dill Salad Sandwich
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Mains). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Pick Up Limes; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. In a large bowl, mash the chickpeas with a potato masher or fork until flaky, with a few chunks left for texture.
2. Add the rest of the filling ingredients and mix well. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
3. Pile onto bread with your favourite sandwich fillings, or serve with crackers and vegetables, or on top of a salad.

name: Texan-Style Vegan Chili
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Mains). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Brand New Vegan; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Chop the onions and peppers and put them in a large soup pot or Dutch oven with a splash of the vegetable broth. Sauté over medium heat, adding broth as needed to stop sticking, until soft and translucent.
2. Add the minced garlic and stir about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
3. Add the meat substitute (if using) or the dry, uncooked bulgur and stir a few minutes until heated through.
4. Add the tomatoes, tomato sauce and the rest of the broth, then the spices, and stir well.
5. Stir in all the beans and the jalapeños.
6. If it looks thin, sprinkle 1–2 tablespoons of masa harina over the top and stir it in; it thickens the chili and adds a mild corn-tortilla flavour.
7. Bring to a slow boil, then lower the heat, cover and simmer 15–30 minutes (make sure the bulgur is tender if you used it).

name: Lemon-Parsley Panko Crusted Salmon

instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 425°F.
2. In a small bowl, mix the panko, parsley, lemon zest, ½ teaspoon salt and ½ teaspoon pepper. Drizzle in the olive oil and stir until all the crumbs are evenly moistened.
3. Lay the salmon fillets skin-side down on a board. Brush the tops generously with mustard and season well with salt and pepper. Press a thick layer of the panko mixture onto each fillet; the mustard is the glue.
4. Heat the vegetable oil over medium-high in a 12-inch cast-iron skillet (or another large heavy, ovenproof pan). When the oil is very hot, add the fillets skin-side down and sear 3–4 minutes without moving them, to brown and crisp the skin.
5. Move the whole pan to the oven and bake 5–7 minutes, until the salmon is almost cooked through and the crumbs are browned.
6. Take it out, cover loosely with foil and rest 5–10 minutes (it finishes cooking as it rests). Serve hot or at room temperature with lemon wedges.

instructions:
1. Set a rack in the top third of the oven and heat to 450°F. Halve the lemon: slice one half into thin rounds and pick out the seeds; keep the other half for the sauce.
2. In a large bowl, whisk the garlic, 2 teaspoons chopped oregano and ⅓ cup oil. Pat the chicken dry with paper towels and add it to the bowl with the onions and lemon slices. Season with salt and pepper and toss to coat.
3. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large heavy skillet (cast iron is best) over medium-high. Lift the chicken out of the bowl (leave the onions and lemon behind) and cook it skin-side down, without moving, for 5–7 minutes, until the skin is deep golden and crisp. Move to a plate; it won't be cooked through yet.
4. In the same pan, cook the onions and lemon slices about 5 minutes, turning now and then, until the onions have some colour and the lemons have shrivelled slightly.
5. Nestle the chicken back in, skin-side up, and put the pan in the oven. Roast 16–20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the onions are soft but still hold their shape.
6. Meanwhile, stir the yogurt, feta and remaining 2 tablespoons oil together in a medium bowl. Squeeze in the juice from the reserved lemon half, add 2 tablespoons water and mix well. Season with salt.
7. Spread the tomatoes on a platter and salt them. Arrange the chicken, onions and lemon slices on top with tongs, pour over the pan juices and scatter with oregano leaves. Serve the feta sauce on the side.

name: Thai Tuna Laab
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Mains). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Feed the Pudge; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Prep: slice the red onion thinly along the grain into strips (soak 5 minutes in cold water and drain if you want to tame the raw bite). Pick the mint leaves off the stems. Finely chop the green onions and cilantro.
2. Toasted rice powder: put 2 tablespoons of uncooked sticky rice and 2–3 kaffir lime leaves in a dry pan over medium heat. Stir often for 5–7 minutes, until the rice is golden brown and smells nutty. Take off the heat, discard the lime leaves, and grind the rice to a coarse powder in a mortar and pestle or spice grinder.
3. Sauce: in a small bowl, stir together 1 tablespoon fish sauce, the juice of 2 limes, 1 teaspoon sugar and 1 tablespoon crushed dried chili until the sugar dissolves.
4. Drain the canned tuna and put it in a mixing bowl with the red onion, green onions, cilantro and mint.
5. Pour over the sauce and mix well, then add the toasted rice powder and toss gently.
6. Serve at room temperature with lettuce or cabbage leaves or cucumber slices for scooping, and sticky rice on the side.

name: Sheet Pan Chicken Shawarma with Garlic Sauce

instructions:
1. In a medium bowl or zip-top bag, combine the lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, kosher salt, pepper, cumin, smoked paprika, turmeric, red pepper flakes and a dash of cinnamon. Add the chicken thighs, coat well and refrigerate at least 1 hour (or overnight).
2. While it marinates, make the garlic sauce: whisk the mayonnaise, Greek yogurt, garlic, salt, pepper and lemon juice in a small bowl. Refrigerate until needed.
3. Heat the oven to 425°F. Lay the chicken thighs on an 18×13-inch sheet pan, arrange the onions around them and spoon the leftover marinade over the onions.
4. Roast 30–45 minutes depending on the size of the thighs, until they reach 170°F inside.
5. Sprinkle with parsley and rest 5 minutes, then slice against the grain. Put the slices back on the pan and toss them in the juices and spices.
6. Serve with the garlic sauce.

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Postpartum). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Flavorful Life; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Pulse the oats in a food processor until fine, like flour. (You can leave them whole, but oat flour gives a better texture.)
2. In a large bowl, stir together the oat flour, 4 cups flour (spooned and levelled), 1½ teaspoons baking soda, 1½ teaspoons baking powder, 1½ teaspoons kosher salt, ½ cup brewer's yeast, ½ cup ground flaxseed and ½ teaspoon cinnamon.
3. In a stand mixer with the paddle, cream 2½ sticks butter and ½ cup coconut oil about 2 minutes, until light. Add 1½ cups brown sugar and 1½ cups sugar and beat 4–5 minutes more, until very light and fluffy.
4. Beat in the eggs one at a time, about 30 seconds each. Add 4 teaspoons vanilla and 1 teaspoon lemon juice.
5. Add the dry ingredients gradually, mixing just until combined. It's a huge batch, so the bowl will be full. Stir in the chocolate by hand.
6. Scoop 2–3 tablespoon mounds onto a parchment-lined tray and freeze 1–2 hours.
7. To store, move the frozen dough balls to a freezer bag; they keep up to 6 months.
8. To bake, heat the oven to 350°F. Space the dough balls 2 inches apart on a lined tray and bake 11–13 minutes, until just barely golden on top. Slightly underbaked is better than overbaked; watch closely, and adjust the time if you change the size.

7. Bake 11–14 minutes with coconut sugar, or 14–17 minutes with brown sugar, until the centres no longer look wet. They'll be very soft but firm up as they sit.
