about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Desserts). Steps written in our own words, adapted from House & Garden; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan / 325°F / gas 3). Line the bottoms of three 23 cm (9-inch) round cake tins with parchment, then butter and lightly flour the parchment and sides (or use nonstick spray).
2. In a large bowl, beat the butter with an electric mixer on medium until smooth. Add both sugars and beat about 3 minutes, until fluffy. Beat in the eggs, then the red wine and vanilla. It may look a bit curdled; that's fine.
3. Sift the flour, cocoa, bicarbonate of soda, baking powder, cinnamon and salt right over the wet mixture. Mix until about three-quarters combined, then finish folding by hand with a rubber spatula so you don't overwork it.
4. Divide the batter evenly between the tins. Bake about 25 minutes, until a tester in the centre comes out clean; the tops should look smooth and shiny.
5. Cool in the tins on a rack about 10 minutes, then turn out and cool completely on the rack.
6. If the layers have domed, level the tops with a long serrated knife held flat, using gentle sawing strokes.
7. For the frosting, beat the mascarpone with the icing sugar, a pinch of salt and the vanilla on medium for 1–2 minutes, until light and fluffy. Don't overbeat, or mascarpone can turn grainy.
8. Put one layer on a cake stand, spread with a third of the frosting, and repeat with the other two layers. Chill until ready to serve.

name: Almond Brownie Cookies
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Desserts). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Pick Up Limes; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Stir the ground flaxseed and water together in a small bowl and set aside to thicken.
2. Fill a saucepan halfway with water and bring to a boil. Set a large heatproof bowl on top, add the chocolate and coconut oil, and stir until melted and smooth.
3. Stir in the brown sugar, then carefully take the bowl off the heat (it'll be hot).
4. Stir in the flax mixture, almonds and vanilla.
5. Sift in the flour, baking powder and salt and stir just until combined; don't overmix. Let the dough rest at room temperature 15 minutes.
6. Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and line a baking tray.
7. Roll about 1½ tablespoons of dough per cookie into balls. Place them on the tray about 5 cm apart and flatten into discs about 1 cm thick; they don't spread much on their own.
8. Press a few bits of chopped chocolate and almond onto each, if you like. Bake 10–11 minutes.
9. Sprinkle with flaky salt, cool on the tray a few minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool completely.

name: Ina Garten’s Tiramisu

ingredients.ingredient: extra-large egg yolks, at room temperature 1/4 cup sugar 1/2 cup good dark rum, divided 1 1/2 cups brewed espresso, divided 16 to 17 ounces mascarpone cheese 30 Italian ladyfingers, or savoiardi Bittersweet chocolate, shaved or grated Confectioners’ sugar
ingredients.notes: at room temperature 1/4 cup sugar 1/2 cup good dark rum, divided 1 1/2 cups brewed espresso, divided 16 to 17 ounces mascarpone cheese 30 Italian ladyfingers, or savoiardi Bittersweet chocolate, shaved or grated Confectioners’ sugar (optional)

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Desserts). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Barefoot Contessa; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Put the egg yolks and sugar in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk. Whisk on high for 5 minutes, until very thick and pale yellow.
2. Turn the mixer down to medium and add ¼ cup rum, ¼ cup espresso and the mascarpone. Whisk until smooth.
3. In a shallow bowl, mix the remaining ¼ cup rum with the remaining 1¼ cups espresso.
4. Dip one side of each ladyfinger quickly into the espresso mixture (just one side, so they don't go soggy) and lay them in a single layer across the bottom of a 9×12×2-inch dish.
5. Pour half the mascarpone cream evenly over them. Add a second layer of dipped ladyfingers, then the rest of the cream. Smooth the top.
6. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight to set.
7. Before serving, scatter shaved chocolate over the top and dust lightly with powdered sugar if you like.

name: No-Bake Marbled Pumpkin Pie

ingredients.ingredient: raw or lightly toasted pecans, almonds, or other nuts
ingredients.notes: 270 g), almonds, or other nuts (or a combination

ingredients.ingredient: raw cashews, covered in cool water and soaked 4-12 hours
ingredients.notes: (120 g), covered in cool water and soaked 4-12 hours

ingredients.ingredient: plus 2 tablespoons  melted and warm extra-virgin coconut oil )

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Desserts). Steps written in our own words, adapted from The Bojon Gourmet; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Crust: in a food processor or blender, pulse the pecans, almonds, ginger, cinnamon and salt until finely ground; stop before it turns into nut butter. Drizzle in the maple syrup and coconut oil and pulse just until the mixture starts to clump.
2. Tip it into a 9-inch tart pan with a removable bottom. With damp fingers, press it evenly across the bottom and up the sides. Freeze while you make the filling.
3. Filling: wipe out the processor or blender. Add the soaked, drained cashews, maple syrup and salt and pulse until the cashews are ground. Add the water and vanilla and blend on high about 3 minutes, scraping down the sides, until silky smooth. Add the melted coconut oil and blend just to combine.
4. Scoop out ¼ cup (60 ml) of this cashew cream and set it aside for the swirl.
5. Add the squash purée, carrot juice, grated ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg and cloves to the blender and blend on low just until combined.
6. Put the frozen crust on a platter or rimmed baking sheet so it's easy to move. Pour in the squash filling. Drop small spoonfuls of the reserved cashew cream over the surface and swirl gently with a chopstick, toothpick or knife tip. Stop early, or the swirls blur.
7. Chill at least 4 hours (up to 2 days) until completely set. If it's too soft to slice cleanly, give it a short stint in the freezer (thaw before serving).
8. To unmould, set the tart on a large can or upside-down ramekin and gently ease the ring down. Slice into wedges with a large sharp knife, wiping it clean between cuts.

name: Cherry Chocolate Cheesecake

ingredients.ingredient: Note can be swapped for 125g  store bought cherry jam
raw cashews, soaked 4 hours in water
Labneh made from 250g  yoghurt  or 3/4 cup store bought cream cheese

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Desserts). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Panacea's Pantry; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Grease and line a 7-inch round springform tin (or one with a removable base). If you're making homemade labneh, start it about 4 hours ahead, while the cashews soak.
2. Cherry jam: put the cherries and a splash of water in a small saucepan over low-medium heat for about 5 minutes, until soft and juicy. Turn off the heat, mash with a fork, and stir in the chia seeds and sugar. Leave it to thicken and cool.
3. Base: blend the pecans, salt, coconut flour, sugar and cacao in a food processor until fine. Melt the butter, add it, and pulse until it looks like moist crumbs. Tip into the tin and press into an even, firm layer with the back of a spoon.
4. Once the jam is at room temperature, spread it over the base, leaving a 2 cm (¾-inch) border all the way around the edge. Refrigerate while you make the filling.
5. Filling: drain the cashews and blend on high with the labneh (or cream cheese), milk, cacao powder and coconut sugar for about 1 minute, until silky smooth. Scrape it all into a mixing bowl.
6. Put the butter and chopped chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Bring about 2 cm of water to a boil in a small saucepan, turn it down, and set the bowl on top (it should sit on the rim, not in the water). Stir now and then until fully melted, then pour into the cashew mixture and fold until evenly coloured.
7. Pour the filling gently over the jam layer and smooth the top. Refrigerate at least 4 hours, or overnight.
8. Slice with a hot, sharp knife (dip it in hot water and wipe between cuts). Let slices sit a few minutes to take the chill off, and serve with cream and fresh cherries.

name: Veggie Crinkle Cake

ingredients.ingredient: store-bought phyllo pastry, thawed in the fridge overnight
extra virgin olive oil, plus more for greasing and topping
ingredients.notes: plus more for greasing and topping

ingredients.ingredient: granulated garlic or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Desserts). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Carolina Gelen; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Brush the bottom of a 12-inch cast-iron skillet or round baking dish with oil.
2. Unroll the phyllo and lay the sheets flat. Working two sheets at a time, scrunch them together loosely (like crumpled fabric) and arrange them in the skillet in a circle. Repeat until the bottom is completely covered in crinkled phyllo.
3. Tuck the sliced vegetables in between the folds of phyllo.
4. Drizzle ¼ cup olive oil over the top and sprinkle with salt. Bake 35–40 minutes, until golden and crisp to the touch.
5. Take it out and lower the oven to 350°F (175°C).
6. In a medium bowl, whisk the egg yolks, milk, fennel, paprika, garlic, a few grinds of black pepper and a big pinch of salt.
7. Pour this custard evenly over the baked phyllo and vegetables, letting it seep into the gaps.
8. Return to the oven and bake 25–30 minutes, until the custard is set.
9. Meanwhile, mix the garlic, parsley and 2 tablespoons olive oil in a small bowl. Brush it all over the top as soon as the cake comes out of the oven.
10. Cut into wedges and serve warm.

name: Banana Nut Muffins
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Desserts). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Love and Lemons; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 12-cup muffin tin or line it with paper liners.
2. In a large bowl, whisk the mashed banana, maple syrup, coconut oil, eggs and vanilla.
3. In a medium bowl, whisk the all-purpose and whole-wheat flours, baking soda, cinnamon, salt and nutmeg.
4. Add the dry ingredients to the wet and stir just until no dry streaks remain; overmixing makes muffins tough. Fold in the walnuts.
5. Divide the batter between the cups (a heaping ⅓ cup each) and sprinkle the oats on top.
6. Bake 20–25 minutes, until the tops spring back when pressed and a toothpick comes out with just a few moist crumbs.
7. Cool in the tin 10 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool completely.

name: Cranberry-Lime Pie

ingredients.ingredient: 12-ounce package fresh  cranberries, plus 4 ounces  for serving
unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into pieces
ingredients.notes: (1½ sticks) unsalted, room temperature, cut into pieces

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Gluten-Free Baking). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Bon Appétit; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Crust: heat the oven to 350°F. Pulse the cookies in a food processor until very finely ground (about 1 cup). Add the pecans and pulse until fine, then add the butter and brown sugar and pulse to combine.
2. Tip into a deep 9-inch pie dish and press firmly over the bottom and up the sides with the bottom of a measuring cup. Bake 10–15 minutes, until firm and slightly darker. If the sides slump, press them back up while warm. Let cool. (The crust can be made a day ahead; wrap tightly and keep at room temperature.)
3. Filling: in a large saucepan, bring 12 oz cranberries, 1 cup sugar and ¼ cup water to a boil over medium-high. Lower the heat and simmer 12–15 minutes, until the berries burst and most of the liquid has cooked off. Let cool, then purée in a blender until very smooth.
4. Set a heatproof bowl over a saucepan of barely simmering water (the bowl shouldn't touch the water). Add the purée, eggs, egg yolks, lemon zest, lime juice, salt, ½ cup sugar and 1 teaspoon lime zest. Stir constantly with a rubber spatula, scraping the sides often, for 8–10 minutes, until the curd thickens and coats the spatula. Let it cool until just warm.
5. With an electric mixer on medium-high, beat the curd while adding the butter one piece at a time, letting each piece blend in before adding the next. Keep beating about 5 minutes, until it's lighter in colour and texture. Scrape into the crust and chill about 2 hours, until firm.
6. Sugared cranberries: in a small saucepan, bring ½ cup sugar and ½ cup water to a simmer over medium, stirring to dissolve. Add the remaining 4 oz cranberries and cook about 1 minute, just until they start to soften. Lift them out with a slotted spoon onto a wire rack set in a rimmed baking sheet and chill 20–30 minutes, until no longer sticky.
7. Toss the last ½ cup sugar with 1 teaspoon lime zest, roll the cranberries in it, and pile them on the pie. Serve with whipped cream.

The pie (without topping) can be made 2 days ahead; cover once firm and keep chilled. Let it sit out 2 hours before serving.

name: Hummus

ingredients.ingredient: extra virgin olive oil, parsley, chopped kalamata olives, for garnish
ingredients.notes: parsley, chopped kalamata olives, for garnish

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Dips + Sauces). Steps written in our own words, adapted from The Edgy Veg; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. The night before: put the dried chickpeas in a large container with 1 tablespoon sea salt, 1 teaspoon baking soda and 4 cups water. Stir to dissolve and soak in the fridge overnight.
2. Next day, rinse the chickpeas in cold water and pick out any stones or debris. Put them in a pressure cooker (Instant Pot) with 1 teaspoon salt, 1 teaspoon baking soda, the bay leaf, 1 garlic clove and the half onion. Cover with water by 2 inches.
3. Cook on high pressure for 10 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 15 minutes.
4. While they cook, purée 4 garlic cloves with the lemon juice and salt in a food processor. Scrape down so the garlic is sitting in the lemon juice and leave it to mellow.
5. When the chickpeas are done, remove the onion and bay leaf. Drain, saving the cooking liquid. Keep the cooked garlic clove.
6. Add the tahini to the food processor and blend, adding reserved chickpea liquid one tablespoon at a time until the tahini is smooth and pale.
7. Add the chickpeas, the cooked garlic clove and the cumin. Blend for 5–8 minutes, adding chickpea liquid a tablespoon at a time, until very smooth and light. It takes longer than you'd expect. Taste and adjust the salt.
8. Spread in a bowl, drizzle with olive oil and top with chopped parsley (and ful or whole chickpeas if you like). Serve with sliced onion and pita.

name: Pad Kee Mao Sauce

ingredients.notes: or ⅛ red bell pepper, chopped

ingredients.ingredient: A dash black or dark soy sauce

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Dips + Sauces). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Hot Thai Kitchen; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Cook one portion at a time for the best char, so split your prep into portions before you start.
2. Stir the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.
3. Loosen the rice noodles. If they're cold, hard and stuck together, they'll snap, so warm them first: split into 3–4 small bundles, spread on a large plate and microwave at 70% power, stopping every minute to move them around. Once soft, pull them apart and divide into portions.
4. Pound the Thai chilies in a mortar and pestle until fine, then add the garlic and spur chilies and pound to a rough paste.
5. Set up before you cook: keep the firm vegetables (plus grachai and young peppercorns, if using) together in one bowl; keep the basil and leafy greens in another; put a tablespoon in the sauce and a teaspoon in the sugar; have an empty bowl ready for the cooked protein.
6. Heat about 2 tablespoons oil in a well-seasoned or nonstick wok over high heat until very hot. Add the protein in a single layer and sear until browned on one side, then flip or toss and cook until done. Remove to the bowl.
7. Put the wok back on the burner with the heat off. Add the chili-garlic paste (and a little more oil if needed), then turn the heat to medium and stir just until the bits of garlic turn golden.
8. Add the firm vegetables, turn the heat to high and stir-fry about 30 seconds.
9. Add the noodles, drizzle over 2 tablespoons sauce and sprinkle 1¼ teaspoons sugar per portion. Toss until the noodles are evenly coated and the sauce is absorbed. For a darker colour, add a little dark soy sauce now.
10. Return the protein and toss. Then leave the noodles alone for 15–20 seconds so they char in spots; flip and repeat 1–2 more times.
11. Turn off the heat and toss in the basil and leafy greens just until wilted. Serve right away.

name: Roasted Eggplant

ingredients.ingredient: eggplant, top removed and cut into slices the long way
ingredients.notes: large, top removed and cut into slices the long way

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Sides + Snax). Steps written in our own words, adapted from The Edgy Veg; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Set a rack over a rimmed baking sheet and lay out the eggplant slices. Salt them generously on both sides and leave at least 30 minutes, ideally an hour, to draw out the bitter liquid. (This salt is for drawing out moisture, not seasoning, so don't hold back.)
2. Heat the oven to 400°F.
3. Wipe off the salt and liquid with a clean towel or paper towels, pressing firmly to get as much moisture out as possible. Empty and dry the sheet.
4. Cut each slice in half crosswise. Brush every piece all over with olive oil and lay them on a lined baking sheet.
5. Sprinkle with salt, garlic powder and paprika. Work quickly: eggplant soaks up oil like a sponge, so get it into the oven as soon as it's oiled and seasoned.
6. Roast 40–60 minutes, until golden brown and crisp outside and soft inside.
7. Serve drizzled with tahini sauce and parsley as a side, spread on hot bread, tossed through pasta (alla Norma), tucked into a sabich sandwich or on tahini toast.

name: Frizzled Chickpeas with Feta and Scallions

ingredients.ingredient: can chick peas, drained and rinsed
shallots, peeled and thinly sliced into rings
ingredients.notes: peeled and thinly sliced into rings

ingredients.ingredient: leek, white and light green parts
ingredients.notes: large, white and light green parts finely chopped, chopped, finely

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Sides + Snax). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Lemon and Salt; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan (nonstick is easiest) over medium-high. Add the drained, rinsed chickpeas and leave them alone for a few minutes so they start to crisp. Use that time to slice the shallots, chop the leek and slice the garlic.
2. Give the pan a shake. Once the chickpeas are browning nicely, add the shallots, leek and garlic and season with salt, pepper and red pepper flakes.
3. Keep the heat high enough for a lively sizzle but not so high that things scorch; you want the shallots and leek to fry crisp, not burn or go soft and jammy. Stir now and then.
4. When the shallots are golden brown and the chickpeas are crisp, take the pan off the heat. Toss in the feta and scallion and tip it all into a bowl.
5. If adding an egg, fry it over easy in the same pan and put it on top.
6. Finish with chives, a few more pepper flakes and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Dukkah
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Sides + Snax). Steps written in our own words, adapted from The Mediterranean Dish; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Put the hazelnuts and almonds in a dry cast-iron pan (no oil). Toast over medium-high, tossing often, until golden brown. Tip them into a dish.
2. Add the sesame seeds to the same pan and toast over medium, tossing, until golden. This only takes a minute or two, so watch closely.
3. Put the toasted nuts and sesame seeds in a small food processor with the pistachios, fennel seeds, spices and a good pinch of kosher salt.
4. Pulse in short bursts for a few seconds, just until coarse and crumbly. Don't over-process; it should stay chunky, not turn into a powder or paste.
5. Serve in a bowl next to a bowl of good olive oil and bread (pita or Jerusalem bagel): dip the bread in oil, then in dukkah. It also makes a good topping for salads, soups, chicken, meat and roasted vegetables.

Keeps up to 2 weeks in a tightly closed jar.

name: Mediterranean Marinated Chickpeas with Basil and Feta

ingredients.ingredient: cans  chickpeas, rinsed and drained, or 3 cups cooked chickpeas

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Sides + Snax). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Cookie and Kate; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. In a medium serving bowl, combine the drained chickpeas, chopped roasted red peppers, crumbled feta and torn basil.
2. In a small bowl, whisk the olive oil, vinegar, honey, garlic, oregano, salt, pepper and red pepper flakes.
3. Pour the dressing over the chickpeas and stir well.
4. Cover and refrigerate at least 30 minutes so the chickpeas soak up the flavour.

Keeps up to 5 days in the fridge.

name: Sweet Potato Waffles
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Brekky). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Feel Good Foodie; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Preheat the waffle iron according to its instructions.
2. In a medium bowl, whisk the flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt.
3. In a large bowl, whisk the mashed sweet potato, milk, sugar, oil and eggs until smooth and well combined.
4. Add the dry ingredients to the wet and stir just until combined; a few lumps are fine.
5. Spray the hot waffle iron with cooking spray. Pour in about ⅓ cup batter (adjust for your iron) and cook 6–8 minutes, until golden brown and cooked through.
6. Serve warm with maple syrup.

name: Savory Sardine Salad
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Salads). Steps written in our own words, adapted from All Ways Delicious; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Drain the sardines, keeping the oil from the can. Pick out any larger bones if you like (the small ones are soft and edible), then chop the sardines.
2. In a small serving bowl, mix the sardines and their oil with the lemon juice, finely chopped onion, parsley, salt and pepper.
3. Taste and add more salt, pepper or lemon as needed.

name: Italian Pasta Salad with Prosciutto

ingredients.ingredient: uncooked brown rice farfalle or rotini

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Salads). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Fun Without FODMAPs; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Cook the pasta according to the package. Drain and rinse under cold water until completely cool, then drain well.
2. Put the pasta in a large bowl with the cucumber, tomatoes, olives, chives, prosciutto and any other mix-ins. Stir and set aside.
3. Put all the red wine vinaigrette ingredients except the salt in a blender and blend until well mixed. Season with salt to taste.
4. Pour the vinaigrette over the pasta and stir well. Serve right away, or refrigerate until needed.

name: Moroccan Lentil Salad

ingredients.ingredient: red wine vinegar, or sherry or apple cider vinegar
ingredients.notes: or sherry or apple cider vinegar

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Salads). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Feasting at Home; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Cook the lentils according to the package, until tender but still holding their shape. Drain and let cool. (You can do this ahead.)
2. If raw onion is too sharp for you, chop it and soak in a bowl of cold salted water while you prep the rest, then drain.
3. In a large bowl, combine the lentils, celery, chopped apricots, almonds, drained onion, herbs and orange zest.
4. Add the dressing ingredients straight into the bowl and toss. (If using honey, mix the dressing separately first so it dissolves.)
5. Taste and add salt, chili flakes if you like, and more orange juice. It usually needs a little more salt after it sits for a while.

name: Zucchini, Pea & Goat Cheese Orzo Salad
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Salads). Steps written in our own words, adapted from All Types of Bowls; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 350°F.
2. Toss the zucchini and onions with 2 tablespoons olive oil, salt and pepper on a baking sheet. Tuck the garlic cloves, still in their skins, around the pan. Roast 25–30 minutes, stirring halfway, until soft and lightly browned.
3. Meanwhile, bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the orzo according to the package. With 5 minutes left, add the frozen peas to the same pot. Drain and put in a large bowl.
4. Add the roasted zucchini and onions. Squeeze the soft roasted garlic out of its skins, chop it finely and add it to the bowl.
5. Add the rest of the olive oil, the lemon juice and zest, salt, pepper, thyme and crumbled goat cheese.
6. Toss everything together and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Low FODMAP Orzo Salad
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Salads). Steps written in our own words, adapted from FODMAP Everyday; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Cook the orzo in a large pot of salted water until al dente. Drain well and put it in a large bowl. While it's still warm, drizzle over just enough of the lemon dressing to coat; warm orzo absorbs it best.
2. Let it cool to room temperature.
3. Wash, dry and trim the cucumbers and slice them thinly crosswise. Add them to the orzo with the halved tomatoes, dill, parsley, scallion greens (the green parts only keep it low-FODMAP) and lemon zest.
4. Add enough dressing to coat, then taste and season well with salt and pepper.
5. Let it sit 15 minutes for the flavours to come together, then serve.

Best made fresh. If you refrigerate it (up to 24 hours, airtight), bring it fully back to room temperature and refresh with a little more dressing before serving.

name: Vegan Chickpea “Tuna” Salad
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Salads). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Sarah's Vegan Kitchen; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then shake off as much water as you can (wet chickpeas make a watery salad).
2. Put them in a bowl and mash with a fork or potato masher, leaving some texture.
3. Add the rest of the ingredients and stir to combine. Add a little more vegan mayo if you want it creamier.
4. Season with salt and pepper; how much depends on how salty your chickpeas and mayo are.
5. Eat right away on a sandwich or as a vegan "tuna" melt.

Keeps up to 5 days airtight in the fridge.

name: Korean Hangover Soup (Ppyeo-haejangguk 뼈해장국)
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Soups). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Maangchi; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Bone broth: rinse the ox bones in cold water to wash off any bone fragments, then soak them in fresh cold water to draw out the blood.
2. Bring 6 quarts water to a rolling boil in a heavy pot over high heat. Drain the bones and add them to the boiling water.
3. Cover, lower to medium and keep it boiling about 4 hours. Check the level now and then; if it drops below 6 cups, top up with cold water. Keep going until the broth is milky white and you still have at least 6 cups.
4. Take off the heat and strain, separating the bones from the broth.
5. When the bones are cool enough to handle, pick off any ligaments and bits of meat and keep them in a bowl.
6. Cool the broth, then refrigerate several hours or overnight until the fat sets on top. (In a hurry, set the bowl of broth in a larger bowl of ice water, changing the ice once.) Skim off the solid yellowish fat with a spoon.
7. Pressure-cooker shortcut: cook the bones with 10 cups water for about 30 minutes, cool, skim the fat, then boil the broth in a pot over medium with more water as needed until milky and you have 6 cups.
8. Soup: bring a large pot of water to a boil and blanch the napa cabbage 5 minutes. Drain, rinse in cold water a couple of times, squeeze out the water and chop into small pieces.
9. In a bowl, mix the cabbage with the doenjang, garlic, green chili and fish sauce by hand or with a wooden spoon.
10. Put the cabbage mixture in a large pot with 6 cups of the bone broth and the reserved meat and ligament bits. Cover and cook 20 minutes over medium-high, then lower the heat and cook 10 minutes more.
11. Ladle into bowls, sprinkle with chopped green onion, and serve with rice, kimchi, gochugaru and other side dishes.

name: Kimchi
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Sides + Snax). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Maangchi; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Prep the cabbage: trim the core if it sticks out a lot. To halve each cabbage without shredding the tight inner leaves, cut a short slit in the base, then pull the two halves apart by hand. Cut a slit through the core of each half about 2 inches up from the stem, so the leaves loosen but stay attached.
2. Dunk the halves in a large basin of water to wet them. Lift every leaf and sprinkle salt between them, using more salt near the thick stem ends.
3. Let them sit 2 hours, turning them over every 30 minutes so they salt evenly. You can ladle the salty water from the bottom of the basin over them now and then.
4. After 2 hours, rinse the cabbage several times under cold running water to remove the salt and any grit. As you wash, split each half into quarters along the slits you cut earlier. Cut off the cores, give a final rinse, and set in a colander over a basin to drain well.
5. Make the porridge: in a small pot, mix the water and sweet rice flour with a wooden spoon. Cook over medium heat about 10 minutes, stirring, until it starts to bubble. Add the sugar and stir 1 minute more. Take off the heat and let it cool completely.
6. Pour the cooled porridge into a large bowl. Add the garlic, ginger, onion, fish sauce, fermented salted shrimp and hot pepper flakes and mix with the wooden spoon until it's a thin, even paste.
7. Mix in the radish, carrot and green onion (and Asian chives and water dropwort if using).
8. Working in a large bowl (wear gloves; the pepper stings), spread paste over every leaf of each cabbage quarter. Fold each coated quarter over on itself into a small bundle and pack it into a jar, plastic container or onggi.
9. Eat right away as fresh kimchi, or let it sit at room temperature a few days to ferment, then refrigerate.

name: Cubed Radish Kimchi (Kkakdugi 깍두기)
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Korean Feast). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Maangchi; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Peel the radish, rinse under cold water and pat dry. Cut into ¾–1-inch cubes and put them in a large bowl.
2. Add the kosher salt and sugar, mix well and let stand 30 minutes; the radish will release liquid.
3. Drain the liquid into a small bowl and keep it.
4. Add the garlic, ginger, green onions, fish sauce, hot pepper flakes and ⅓ cup of the reserved radish liquid to the radish.
5. Mix well (gloves help) until every cube is evenly red and looks juicy.
6. Pack into a glass jar, pressing down firmly to push out air pockets between the cubes.
7. Eat right away, or refrigerate for later.
8. For fermented kkakdugi, leave the jar at room temperature 1–2 days (less in a warm kitchen). When you see small bubbles and it smells pleasantly sour, move it to the fridge.

name: Japchae (Stir-fried Noodles and Vegetables 잡채)

ingredients.ingredient: pork belly, pork shoulder, beef, or chicken, cut into strips
ingredients.notes: pork shoulder, beef, or chicken, cut into strips (optional)

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Korean Feast). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Maangchi; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Ahead of time, soak the sweet potato noodles (dangmyeon) and the dried wood ear mushrooms in warm water until soft (about 30 minutes, or per the package).
2. If using meat: mix it with the soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil by hand until the sugar dissolves. Cover and rest 5 minutes. Cook in a hot skillet, stirring with a wooden spoon, 4–5 minutes until cooked through. Set aside.
3. Egg garnish: whisk the eggs with salt, then pour through a strainer so it's completely smooth (discard the stringy bits). Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high, swirl it around, then wipe out the excess with a paper towel. Turn the heat to low, pour in the egg and tilt the pan so it spreads into a thin circle covering the bottom. Cook about 1 minute, until set underneath but not browned. Flip it, take the pan off the heat and let it finish in the leftover heat for a few minutes.
4. Move the egg sheet to a board, let it cool a few minutes, then slice into thin strips. Cover with plastic wrap so they don't dry out.
5. Seasoning sauce: mix the soy sauce, sugar, black pepper and garlic in a bowl until the sugar dissolves.
6. Drain the wood ear mushrooms, cut off the tough stems, and cut the caps into bite-size pieces. Put them in a large pot with the king oyster mushrooms, carrot and onion.
7. Add ¼ cup vegetable oil and ¼ cup water and mix with your hands until everything is coated in oil; this stops the vegetables from browning in the sauce or burning. Spread the spinach evenly over the top.
8. Drain the noodles, cut them into 5–6-inch lengths with scissors, and lay them on top of the spinach. Drizzle the seasoning sauce over the noodles.
9. Cover and cook 10 minutes over medium-high heat.
10. Uncover and toss everything with a wooden spoon and tongs for 1–2 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the noodles are glossy and soft. Stir in the meat, 1 tablespoon sesame oil and 1 tablespoon sesame seeds.
11. Transfer to a platter and top with the egg strips.

name: Spicy Cucumber Side Dish (Oi-muchim 오이무침)
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Korean Feast). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Maangchi; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Halve the cucumber lengthwise, then cut it on the diagonal into thin slices.
2. Put the cucumber in a large bowl with the onion, green onion, garlic, soy sauce, hot pepper flakes, toasted sesame oil, sesame seeds and sugar.
3. Mix well with a spoon until the sugar dissolves and everything is evenly coated.
4. Serve right away as a side dish with rice, noodles or Korean BBQ. Make only what you'll eat in one sitting; the cucumbers release a lot of liquid as it sits.

name: Chicken Pho

ingredients.ingredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Kosher and freshly ground black pepper (to taste)

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Soups). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Damn Delicious; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Set a 6-quart Instant Pot to high sauté. Heat the canola oil and add the onion, ginger and garlic. Cook 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until browned (charring them a bit gives pho its depth).
2. Add the cloves, star anise, cinnamon, cardamom, coriander and peppercorns and stir about 1 minute, until fragrant.
3. Add the chicken thighs, chicken stock, fish sauce, brown sugar, ½ teaspoon salt and 2 cups water.
4. Lock the lid, set to manual/high pressure for 15 minutes. When done, quick-release the pressure following your cooker's instructions.
5. Lift out the chicken and shred it with two forks.
6. Strain the broth through a fine sieve lined with cheesecloth and discard the solids. Skim off any fat from the surface. Season with salt and pepper.
7. Meanwhile, cook the rice noodles in a large pot of boiling water according to the package. Drain well.
8. Divide the noodles and chicken between bowls and ladle the hot broth over. Serve right away with bean sprouts, basil, mint, sliced chili and lime wedges.

name: Vegetarian Italian Wedding Soup

ingredients.notes: large yellow, chopped and divided, large

ingredients.ingredient: baby kale or other dark leafy greens

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Soups). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Radish Rose; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Bean balls: heat the oven to 400°F and coat a baking sheet with cooking spray.
2. In a large bowl, mash the white beans with a potato masher until they're a paste. Mash thoroughly, with very few whole beans left, or the balls won't hold.
3. Stir in ¼ cup of the chopped onion, the breadcrumbs, garlic, nutritional yeast (or flour), olive oil, soy sauce or tamari, dried spices, lemon zest and the egg (if using). Use your hands if needed to mix it all evenly.
4. Roll into golf-ball-size balls and put them on the baking sheet. Spray the tops with a little more oil and bake 30–35 minutes, until golden brown. They're a bit crumbly, so handle gently.
5. Soup: while they bake, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large soup pot over medium. Add the rest of the onion, the carrots, celery and a pinch of salt. Cook 5–7 minutes, stirring, until the onion starts to brown.
6. Add the garlic and pasta and stir about 1 minute.
7. Pour in the broth and simmer 10–15 minutes, until the pasta is tender.
8. Stir in the lemon juice, greens, salt and pepper, and fresh basil, and cook just until the greens wilt.
9. To serve, put 3–4 bean balls in each bowl and gently ladle the soup over them (adding them at the end keeps them from falling apart). Top with grated Parmesan if you like.

name: Carrot Turmeric Ginger Soup
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Soups). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Real Balanced; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 400°F.
2. Halve the peeled carrots lengthwise; if they're thick, cut them in half crosswise too so they roast evenly.
3. Spread them on a baking sheet, drizzle with the olive oil and toss to coat.
4. Roast about 20 minutes, until tender all the way through when pierced with a knife.
5. Put the roasted carrots in a food processor with the turmeric, peeled ginger, rosemary leaves, cinnamon, broth, room-temperature coconut milk, salt and pepper. (The original uses a food processor, not a blender. A food processor gives a thick, slightly textured purée; if you want it silky, use a blender instead, with the lid's centre cap removed and a towel over the hole to let steam escape.)
6. Process on high until well combined and as smooth as you like. Add a splash more broth if it's too thick.
7. Reheat gently if needed. Serve right away, topped with a spoonful of Greek yogurt (lactose-free for low-FODMAP; skip for dairy-free) and fresh parsley.

name: Lemon Coriander Soup
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Soups). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Hebbar's Kitchen; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat 2 teaspoons oil in a large pan or kadai over medium. Add the 2 cloves garlic and 1 inch ginger, both finely chopped, and sauté until fragrant.
2. Add the ½ onion and 2 tablespoons finely chopped coriander stems (they carry a lot of flavour) and sauté 1 minute.
3. Add the finely chopped ½ carrot, 2 tablespoons each cabbage and beans, and 2 tablespoons sweet corn. Sauté 1 minute; keep the vegetables crisp.
4. Pour in 3 cups water, add ½ teaspoon salt and ½ teaspoon pepper, stir and boil 5 minutes.
5. In a small bowl, stir 1 tablespoon cornflour (cornstarch) into ¼ cup water until there are no lumps.
6. Pour the slurry into the soup while stirring and boil 2 more minutes, until slightly thickened.
7. Turn off the heat, then stir in 3 tablespoons chopped coriander leaves and 2 tablespoons lemon juice. Add the lemon off the heat so it stays fresh and doesn't turn bitter.
8. Garnish with more coriander and serve hot.

name: Vegan Lentil Shepherd’s Pie

ingredients.ingredient: kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper
ingredients.notes: kosher and freshly cracked black pepper

ingredients.ingredient: Extra virgin olive oil for baking and finishing

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Mains). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Rainbow Plant Life; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Filling: heat the olive oil in an ovenproof 12-inch sauté pan over medium-high until shimmering. (If your pan isn't ovenproof, you'll move the filling to a baking dish later.)
2. Add the onions with a couple pinches of salt and cook 10–15 minutes, stirring now and then, until most are browned. If they brown unevenly or start to burn, add a splash of water and/or turn the heat down a little. Add the garlic, thyme and rosemary and stir often for 2 minutes.
3. Add the tomato paste and stir constantly for 2–3 minutes, until it darkens. Lower to medium if it starts to catch.
4. Pour in the red wine and scrape up the browned bits. Cook 3–4 minutes, until it has mostly evaporated and no longer smells of alcohol.
5. Stir in the vegetable broth, lentils, bay leaves and paprika. Bring to a boil, then keep at a rapid simmer (steady bubbles across most of the pan) about 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are just tender (not mushy) and most of the liquid is absorbed.
6. Turn the heat to low and stir in the tahini, tamari, balsamic vinegar and vegan Worcestershire (if using) until creamy. Season generously with salt (about 1 teaspoon kosher) and pepper. Remove the bay leaves.
7. Topping: peel the potatoes, rinse, and cut each into eighths. Put them in a large saucepan with the cauliflower, just cover with water, and add 1½ teaspoons kosher salt and the rosemary sprig. Boil about 15 minutes, until both are very soft when poked.
8. Drain well in a colander and discard the rosemary. Pat the potatoes dry, and squeeze the excess water out of the cauliflower (wrap it in a clean towel and wring), or the mash will be watery.
9. Mash the potatoes and cauliflower with the vegan butter (or olive oil), lite coconut milk, nutritional yeast, salt and pepper until smooth.
10. Heat the oven to 375°F. Spread the filling evenly in the pan (or a 3-quart baking dish) and spread the mash over it to the edges. Drizzle with olive oil and season.
11. Bake about 20 minutes, until bubbling at the edges, then broil a few minutes until the top is golden. Watch it closely under the broiler. Sprinkle with chopped parsley to serve.

name: Mediterranean Chicken Tray Bake with Potatoes, Peppers, and Olives

ingredients.ingredient: mini bell peppers, halved and seeded

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Mains). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Allrecipes; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a large rimmed baking sheet with foil.
2. In a large bowl, whisk the olive oil, juice of 1 lemon, vinegar, tarragon, oregano, paprika, salt and pepper.
3. Add the chicken thighs, onion, baby bell peppers and potatoes and stir until everything is evenly coated.
4. Spread it all on the baking sheet in an even layer, with the chicken skin-side up. Scatter the lemon slices over the vegetables, keeping them off the chicken so the skin can brown.
5. Bake about 40 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes are tender.
6. Take it out and top with crumbled feta, chopped parsley and olives.

name: Saffron Asparagus Kitchari
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Mains). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Banyan Botanicals; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Put the saffron in a heavy dry pan over low heat and toast it briefly. Add the ghee, cumin seeds and fenugreek seeds and warm gently until the cumin seeds turn brown.
2. Add the curry leaves, onion and asafoetida and stir. Cook slowly a minute or two, until the onion is tender.
3. Wash the mung dal and rice together, rinsing until the water runs clear. Drain and stir into the spices.
4. Add the water and salt, bring to a simmer, and cook, partly covered, about 1 hour, until the dal and rice are completely soft. Stir now and then and add more water if it gets too thick.
5. Meanwhile, wash the asparagus and cut into 1-inch pieces.
6. About 15 minutes before serving, steam the asparagus until tender, then stir it and the ground cumin into the kitchari. (For extra richness, sauté the asparagus in another tablespoon of ghee instead of steaming.)

name: Falafel
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Mains). Steps written in our own words, adapted from The Mediterranean Dish; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. The day before: put the dried chickpeas (not canned, which make falafel fall apart) and baking soda in a large bowl and cover with water by at least 2 inches. Soak about 18 hours, longer if still very hard. Drain completely and pat dry.
2. Put the chickpeas, herbs, onion, garlic and spices in a large food processor fitted with the blade. Run it in 40-second bursts, scraping down as needed, until it's finely ground and holds together when squeezed, like coarse wet sand rather than a smooth paste.
3. Transfer to a container, cover tightly and refrigerate at least 1 hour (or overnight).
4. Just before frying, stir in the baking powder and sesame seeds.
5. With wet hands, scoop tablespoonfuls and shape into patties about ½ inch thick.
6. Fill a medium saucepan with 3 inches of oil and heat over medium-high until it bubbles gently around a test piece. Fry the patties in batches without crowding, 3–5 minutes, until crisp and medium brown.
7. Drain on a paper-towel-lined plate or colander.
8. Serve hot with other small plates, or tuck into pita with tahini or hummus, arugula, tomato and cucumber.

name: Sicilian Pasta con le Sarde

ingredients.ingredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Kosher and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.ingredient: whole sardines , filleted and cut into 1-inch pieces
ingredients.notes: (about 3/4 pound), filleted and cut into 1-inch pieces

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Mains). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Serious Eats; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the wine until steaming (microwave in a heatproof bowl, or a small saucepan). Add the raisins and saffron (if using) and set aside to plump.
2. Heat 1½ tablespoons olive oil in a small skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add the ground fennel and stir about 20 seconds, until fragrant. Add the breadcrumbs and toss until lightly toasted. Tip into a bowl and season well with salt and pepper.
3. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil for the pasta. Mince half the fennel fronds and keep the other half whole for garnish.
4. In a large skillet, heat the remaining 3 tablespoons olive oil over medium until shimmering. Add the diced onion and fennel bulb and cook about 8 minutes, stirring, until soft. Add the anchovies and stir until they melt into the oil.
5. Add the wine with the raisins and saffron and cook, scraping up any browned bits, until the wine has almost completely evaporated.
6. Add the pine nuts and sardines and stir about 2 minutes, until the sardines are just barely cooked. Take off the heat.
7. Meanwhile, cook the pasta until al dente. Before draining, scoop out at least 1 cup of the cooking water.
8. Add the pasta to the skillet with ¼ cup pasta water. Put back over medium-high heat and toss until the pasta is coated and the excess liquid has cooked off. Add a generous drizzle of fresh olive oil and the minced fronds, toss, and season with salt. Toss in a small handful of the breadcrumbs.
9. If it gets dry, add more pasta water ¼ cup at a time (and more oil if you like). It should be glossy and slick, not sitting in liquid.
10. Divide between bowls, sharing out the sardines, pine nuts and raisins evenly. Top with a generous handful of breadcrumbs and the whole fennel fronds, and serve right away.

name: Chicken Paprikash

ingredients.notes: medium yellow, finely chopped, chopped, finely, medium

ingredients.ingredient: parsley and green onions, for serving

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Mains). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Carolina Gelen; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Put the bite-size chicken pieces in a bowl, season with a big pinch of salt and pepper, add a drizzle of oil and toss to coat. Leave 10 minutes.
2. Heat a glug of oil in a braiser or medium pot over medium. Sear the chicken 2–3 minutes per side, until it has a golden crust; aim for about 80% cooked, since it finishes in the sauce. Move to a plate.
3. Add more oil if needed. Add the onion and cook 3–4 minutes, until golden, soft and translucent. Add the bell peppers and cook 5–7 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft. Turn down to medium-low and keep cooking 4–6 minutes more, until the mixture thickens and starts to caramelize, adding oil if it sticks.
4. Stir in the tomato paste and cook 2–3 minutes, until it darkens. Add the garlic and cook 2 minutes, until fragrant. Add the paprika (and cayenne if using) and cook on low 1–2 minutes to bloom the spices. Keep the heat low; paprika burns and turns bitter quickly.
5. Pour in the coconut milk and stir; it should turn into a silky orange sauce. Add the chicken stock (or stock cube and water), a big pinch of salt and the chicken with its juices.
6. Simmer 15 minutes, stirring now and then. Mix the cornstarch with 1 tablespoon water, stir it in, and simmer 3–5 minutes more, until thick. Taste and adjust the salt.
7. Dumplings: bring a 3–4-quart pot of water to a boil and salt it well. In a bowl, beat the flour, eggs and a pinch of salt hard with a fork into a thick, gooey batter, like a heavy pancake batter.
8. Hold the bowl over the pot and use a spoon to scrape small bits of batter off the edge straight into the boiling water. Repeat until the batter is used up.
9. Simmer 2–4 minutes, until the dumplings have doubled in size. Taste one to check it's cooked, then drain.
10. Serve the dumplings with paprikash spooned over, topped with parsley and green onions.

name: Orange Roast Chicken with Shallots and Fennel
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Mains). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Carolina Gelen; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Marinade: crush the fennel and coriander seeds in a mortar and pestle (or between paper towels with a rolling pin).
2. In a small bowl, rub the sugar, salt and orange zest together with your fingers until the sugar turns bright orange and smells strongly of orange. Add the crushed spices, sage, tarragon, mustard and olive oil and stir into a paste.
3. Spatchcock the chicken: pat it dry with paper towels (save the neck for stock if it came with one). Put it breast-side down and use kitchen shears to cut along both sides of the backbone; remove it (also good for stock). Flip it breast-side up and press firmly on the breastbone with your palm until it cracks and the bird lies flat.
4. Spread the marinade evenly all over, mostly on the skin. Set the chicken on a rack over a tray and leave at room temperature while you prep the rest, or refrigerate uncovered overnight for more flavour.
5. Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C) with a rack in the centre.
6. Cut each orange into 7–8 rounds about ½ inch (1 cm) thick, discarding the ends. Trim the fennel fronds (keep some for serving) and cut each bulb into 5–6 slices through the root. Thinly slice the shallots.
7. Pour the olive oil into a 9×13-inch pan with tall sides: ⅓ cup for a 4-lb chicken, ¼ cup for a 4½-lb one (bigger birds render more fat). Lay the orange slices in a single layer, top with the fennel and scatter over the shallots. Pour in the orange juice and add a big pinch of salt.
8. Set the chicken on top, breast-side up. Poke the skin all over with a knife or skewer to help the fat render, and tuck the wings under the breast so they don't burn.
9. Tent loosely with foil (not touching the skin) and roast 20 minutes.
10. Remove the foil and roast 30–40 minutes more, depending on size. Every 10 minutes or so, spoon the pan juices over the skin to help it crisp. If any spots start to get too dark, cover just those with a scrap of foil.
11. Carve, cutting along the bones to take off the breasts, thighs and wings. Arrange on a platter with the oranges, fennel, shallots and pan juices, and finish with flaky salt and fennel fronds.
12. Optional stock: roast the neck, backbone and any shallot or fennel scraps with plenty of olive oil at 425°F for 10–15 minutes, until darker. Put in a pot with 6 cups water and any other veg scraps, bring to a boil, then simmer until reduced by half. Strain, then refrigerate or freeze.

name: Korean Braised Potatoes
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Korean Feast). Steps written in our own words, adapted from CJ Eats; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Wash and peel the potatoes and cut them into 1-inch pieces.
2. In a bowl, mix the soy sauce, mirin, garlic, sugar and water until the sugar dissolves.
3. Heat 1 tablespoon neutral oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high. Add the potatoes and sauté 4–5 minutes, until they start to turn golden.
4. Pour in the sauce and bring to a simmer. Cook 5–6 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potatoes are fork-tender and the sauce has thickened and coats them.
5. If the sauce is still watery, turn the heat to high and keep stirring until it reduces to a sticky, glossy glaze. Watch it closely at this point, because the sugar can burn.
6. Finish with a drizzle of sesame oil and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

name: Ginger Lemon Switchel (Laborade)
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Postpartum). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Mother Bees; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. In a small heatproof mug or bowl, stir the raw honey into 1 cup hot water until completely dissolved.
2. Pour it into a 1-quart jar or pitcher.
3. Add 3 cups cold or room-temperature water (or sparkling mineral water), the apple cider vinegar, lemon juice, ginger juice or pulp (a garlic press works well for squeezing ginger), trace mineral drops, Rescue Remedy (if using) and sea salt.
4. Stir well and taste. Adjust the honey, lemon or salt to your liking.

Keeps up to 1 week in the fridge. Shake before serving.

name: Lactation Cookies #2
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Postpartum). Steps written in our own words, adapted from How Sweet Eats; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 350°F.
2. In a large bowl, whisk the oats, flour, brewer's yeast, flaxseed, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon and salt.
3. In a stand mixer, beat the butter and coconut oil on medium until creamy. Add the sugar and beat on medium-high 4–5 minutes, until fluffy, scraping down the bowl as needed.
4. Add the egg and egg yolk and beat 2–3 minutes, until combined. Beat in the vanilla.
5. Add the dry ingredients gradually on low speed, mixing just until combined. Stir in the chocolate chips with a spatula until evenly spread through.
6. Scoop 1-inch balls (an ice-cream scoop keeps them even) onto a baking sheet about 2 inches apart.
7. Bake 10–14 minutes, until the bottoms are just golden.
8. Let cool completely before storing in a sealed container.

name: Blueberry Lemon Yogurt Cake
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Desserts). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Smitten Kitchen; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 350°F. Coat a standard loaf pan with nonstick spray, and ideally line it with a parchment sling (overhanging the long sides) for easy removal.
2. In a large bowl, combine the oil and 1 cup of the sugar. Finely grate the zest of all the lemons straight into the bowl and whisk.
3. Whisk in the eggs, vanilla and yogurt until smooth.
4. Sprinkle the baking powder and salt over the batter and whisk thoroughly so they're evenly dispersed (no clumps).
5. Add the flour and blueberries and stir gently just until combined.
6. Pour into the pan and bake 60–75 minutes, until a toothpick in the centre comes out clean.
7. While it bakes, juice the zested lemons; you need ⅓ cup. Heat it in a small saucepan with the remaining 1 tablespoon sugar over medium, just until the sugar dissolves.
8. As soon as the cake comes out, brush the lemon syrup over it. If it isn't soaking in, poke holes all over with a skewer first.
9. Cool completely in the pan. Run a knife around the edge, lift out and dust with powdered sugar if you like. Serve in 1-inch slices.

Keeps 3 days at room temperature or a week in the fridge. Freezes well wrapped tightly; thaw at room temperature for a few hours.

name: Roasted Strawberry Miso Ice Cream

ingredients.notes: or maple syrup or light honey

ingredients.ingredient: a few turns of black pepper

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Desserts). Steps written in our own words, adapted from David Lebovitz; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
2. Hull and quarter the strawberries. In a wide, shallow baking dish with high sides (big enough to hold the berries in a single layer with space around them), toss them with the golden syrup, balsamic vinegar and black pepper.
3. Spread them out and roast on an upper rack 30–40 minutes, stirring once or twice, until very soft and the juices have thickened a lot.
4. Scrape into a bowl and let cool. Then snip the berries into smaller pieces with scissors right in the bowl. (These can be made up to 3 days ahead and refrigerated.)
5. Custard: warm the milk and sugar in a saucepan.
6. While it warms, set up an ice bath: put a 2-quart bowl inside a larger bowl partly filled with ice and water. Set a strainer over the small bowl and pour the cream into it.
7. In a separate bowl, whisk the egg yolks with the miso. Slowly pour in some of the warm milk while whisking constantly (this tempers the yolks so they don't scramble). Scrape it all back into the saucepan.
8. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly and scraping the bottom with a heatproof spatula, until the custard thickens enough to coat the spatula. Don't let it boil.
9. Pour the custard through the strainer into the cream. Stir over the ice until cool, add the vanilla, and refrigerate until thoroughly chilled, ideally overnight.
10. Stir the roasted strawberries into the cold custard and churn in your ice-cream maker according to its instructions. Freeze until firm enough to scoop.

name: Raw Superfood Cheesecake
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Desserts). Steps written in our own words, adapted from This Rawsome Vegan Life; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Line the base of a 6-inch springform pan. (Optional: soaking the cashews and Brazil nuts in water for a few hours, then draining, helps them blend smoother.)
2. Crust: grind the almonds and oats into a flour in a food processor. Add the raisins and process until it forms a sticky, moist dough that holds together when pinched.
3. Press it firmly into the bottom of the pan and put it in the fridge.
4. Vanilla layer: blend the melted cacao butter, cashews, sea salt, lemon juice, maple syrup, vanilla extract and vanilla bean until completely smooth and thick.
5. Mint layer: blend the dates, lemon juice, melted coconut oil, maple syrup, Brazil nuts, green superfood powder (if using) and mint until smooth.
6. Strawberry layer: blend the dried cranberries, almonds, strawberries, beet, maple syrup, lime juice and melted coconut oil until smooth (the beet gives the pink colour).
7. If your blender struggles with any layer, add a little more liquid: maple syrup, melted cacao butter or coconut oil, or lemon/lime juice. Water also works but makes it less creamy.
8. Spread the layers over the crust one after another in whatever order you like, smoothing each one.
9. Freeze overnight to set and let the flavours develop. Let it sit out 10–15 minutes before slicing, and decorate with berries, flowers, nuts, mint leaves or seeds.

name: Vegan (or Not) Brown Butter Peach Cobbler

ingredients.ingredient: vegan vanilla ice cream, to serve

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Desserts). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Rainbow Plant Life; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Set a rack in the middle of the oven and heat to 375°F (190°C).
2. Halve and pit the peaches and cut into slices ¼–½ inch (about 1 cm) thick. Put them in a bowl with the blueberries, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger and cardamom (if using) and toss gently. Leave 30 minutes so the fruit releases its juice.
3. Brown the butter: heat a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over medium. Add the (vegan) butter and spread it up the sides with a spatula as it melts. Once it's foamy and bubbling (2–3 minutes), keep cooking 2 more minutes, stirring often so it doesn't burn, then take the pan off the heat. Vegan butter may not turn golden, but if it smells nutty it's done.
4. Batter: in a medium bowl, whisk the flour, oats, cane sugar, salt and baking powder. Add the oat milk, vanilla and almond extract (if using) and fold with a spatula until just combined.
5. Ladle the batter over the browned butter in spoonfuls in different spots, rather than pouring it all at once; this lets the butter swirl up through it. Don't stir.
6. Arrange the peaches on top, then the blueberries, and spoon over the juices left in the bowl.
7. Bake 45–50 minutes, rotating the pan halfway, until the top is deep golden brown and bubbling.
8. Cool on a rack 10–20 minutes and serve warm, with vanilla ice cream if you like.

name: Strawberry and Matcha Tiramisu
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Desserts). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Life by Mike G; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Roast the strawberries: slice them thinly and roast at 400°F for 15 minutes, until soft and juicy. Set aside to cool.
2. Matcha mascarpone cream: boil some water. Pour it into a large bowl and set a smaller bowl on top, so that only about 40% of the small bowl sits in the water.
3. Put the egg yolks and sugar in the small bowl and whisk until pale and lighter in texture. Lift the bowl off the water, add the mascarpone and whisk until fully combined.
4. In a small bowl, whisk the matcha with 2 tablespoons water until completely smooth with no lumps, then whisk it into the mascarpone mixture.
5. In another bowl, whip the heavy cream to soft peaks (about 5 minutes by hand, 2 by mixer). Gently fold it into the mascarpone mixture.
6. Assemble: pour the milk into a bowl wide enough to dip the ladyfingers. Dip each ladyfinger in the milk for a count of two, then lay it in a square or rectangular dish. Repeat until the bottom is covered in a single layer.
7. Spread 1 cup of the matcha cream evenly over the top, then layer on the cooled roasted strawberries.
8. Add another layer of dipped ladyfingers and top with the rest of the matcha cream, spreading it smooth.
9. Put 2 tablespoons freeze-dried strawberry powder in a fine sieve and tap it evenly over the top.
10. Refrigerate 3–4 hours before serving.

name: Gluten-Free Sandwich Bread

about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Gluten-Free Baking). Steps written in our own words, adapted from Gluten Free on a Shoestring; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Grease or line a 9×5-inch loaf pan (ideally with 4-inch-high sides) or a 1-pound Pullman pan with a lid. You can line the bottom and sides with parchment.
2. In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle, put the flour blend, xanthan gum, instant yeast, cream of tartar and sugar, and whisk together by hand. Add the salt and whisk again.
3. Add the milk, butter, vinegar and egg whites and mix on low, scraping down the sides as needed so there are no dry patches.
4. Turn the mixer to medium-high and beat about 3 minutes. The dough will be thick, smooth and quite wet, and look slightly whipped.
5. Scrape it into the pan and smooth the top with a wet spatula.
6. Cover with lightly oiled plastic wrap (and the Pullman lid if using). Let rise in a warm, draft-free spot 30–45 minutes, until about 50% bigger than when it started; it won't double. It'll take longer in cold, dry weather.
7. Near the end of the rise, heat the oven to 375°F. If the top starts to crack and crater, it's over-proofing; bake it right away.
8. Remove the plastic. If you like, slash the top about ¼ inch deep with a sharp knife, or brush with melted butter and sprinkle with seeds. For a Pullman pan, grease the inside of the lid and slide it back on.
9. Bake on the middle (or top) rack 45 minutes to 1 hour. With a Pullman pan, take the lid off after about 40 minutes and finish baking uncovered.
10. It's done when an instant-read thermometer reads about 205°F inside, a toothpick comes out mostly clean, the crust is thick and brown, and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped.
11. Turn it out of the pan to check. If it's at temperature but still soft on the outside, put it back in the pan (or on a lined sheet), lower the oven to 300°F, and bake up to 20 minutes more until the crust is firm all round.
12. Cool 10 minutes in the pan, then move to a wire rack, remove any parchment, and cool completely (at least 1 hour, ideally 2) before slicing with a serrated knife into about 10 slices.
13. Wrap the cooled loaf (and any cut slices) tightly in plastic wrap to store.

instructions:
1. Put the uncooked rice, water and cinnamon in a blender and blend until the rice is broken up and the water looks milky.
2. Refrigerate overnight so the rice softens and flavours the water.
3. Set a fine-mesh strainer lined with cheesecloth over a pitcher and pour the mixture through, discarding the rice solids. Squeeze the cloth to get all the liquid out.
4. Stir in the plant-based milk, sugar and vanilla until the sugar dissolves.
5. Serve over ice, stirring before pouring since it settles.

instructions:

2. Heat the oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium-low. Add the onion and bell pepper and cook gently about 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until very soft (keep the heat low so they soften rather than brown).
3. Add the garlic and cook 1–2 minutes, until tender. Stir in the cumin, paprika and cayenne and cook 1 minute.

6. Move the skillet to the oven and bake 7–10 minutes, until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
7. Sprinkle with cilantro and serve with hot sauce (and bread for dipping).

name: Cucumber, Watermelon, and Feta Salad
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Salads). Steps written in our own words, adapted from NYT Cooking; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Cut the watermelon into bite-size cubes and chop the tomatoes into similar-size pieces.
2. Peel the cucumber, halve it lengthwise, scoop out the seeds with a spoon and slice it.
3. Slice the red onion very thinly.
4. Put the watermelon, tomatoes, cucumber, onion, olives and crumbled feta in a large bowl and add the chopped parsley and mint.
5. Drizzle with olive oil and a splash of red-wine vinegar, season with salt and pepper, and toss gently. Serve right away, before the watermelon starts to release its juice.

instructions:
1. Heat ¼ cup oil in a large pot over medium. Add the garlic, onion and ginger, season with salt and pepper, and cook 3–5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is translucent and just starting to brown at the edges.
2. Add 1½ teaspoons turmeric, 1 teaspoon red-pepper flakes and the drained chickpeas, and season again. Cook 8–10 minutes, stirring often, so the chickpeas sizzle and fry in the spiced oil until some break down and they get a little browned and crisp. Scoop out about 1 cup of chickpeas and set aside for the topping.
3. With a wooden spoon, crush some of the chickpeas left in the pot against the bottom to release their starch; this is what thickens the stew.
4. Add the coconut milk and stock, season with salt and pepper, and bring to a simmer, scraping up anything stuck to the bottom.
5. Simmer 30–35 minutes, stirring now and then, until thickened. Taste a chickpea or two, not just the broth, to check they're soft and flavourful. Keep simmering if you want it thicker.
6. Stir in the greens, pushing them under the liquid, and cook until wilted and soft: 3 minutes for spinach or chard, up to 7 for kale or collards. Season again.
7. Serve in bowls topped with mint, the reserved chickpeas, a pinch of red-pepper flakes and a good drizzle of olive oil. Yogurt (dusted with turmeric) and toasted pita on the side are optional.

instructions:
1. Cut the kernels off the corn cobs into a bowl. Then scrape each cob firmly with the back of a butter knife so all the milky juice ends up in the bowl and the cobs look dry. (Skip this if using frozen corn.)
2. Heat the olive oil in a large stockpot over medium. Add the shallots, garlic, ginger and chile and cook 3–5 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and fragrant.
3. Add the corn and its juices and cook about 3 minutes, until the corn is brighter and a bit softer.
4. Add the potato pieces and stir 1–2 minutes to coat them.
5. Pour in the vegetable broth and coconut milk. Bring to a boil, then lower to a simmer, cover, and cook 8–10 minutes, until the potatoes are tender all the way through.
6. Roughly blend with an immersion blender so it's creamy but still has some whole kernels, potato chunks and chile flecks. (Or blend about half in a regular blender until smooth and stir it back in.)
7. Season with lime juice and salt. Serve with your choice of toppings.

name: Vegan Chocolate Cupcakes
about: From Ava and Charlie's Digital Cookbook (Desserts). Steps written in our own words, adapted from NYT Cooking; tap Original to see theirs.
instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 350°F and line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.
2. In a large bowl, stir together the soy or rice milk and vinegar and let it sit a minute or two to curdle slightly (this makes a quick vegan buttermilk). Whisk in the sugar, oil and vanilla.
3. In another bowl, mix the flour, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder and salt. Sift this into the wet mixture in two or three additions, whisking after each until no large lumps remain. Don't overmix.
4. Fill the liners about two-thirds full. Bake about 20 minutes, until a toothpick in the centre comes out clean.
5. Cool completely on a wire rack before glazing.
6. Whisk the glaze ingredients until smooth, spread over the cooled cupcakes, and add sprinkles if you like.

instructions:
1. Heat the oven to 425°F.
2. In a large bowl, whisk 4 tablespoons of the oil with 2 teaspoons of the curry powder, 1 teaspoon salt and ½ teaspoon pepper. Toss in the cauliflower and chickpeas until well coated, then spread them in one layer on a rimmed sheet pan.
